__README__: Migrations merged BEFORE scripts/migration-lint.mjs existed, with a written reason each.
RECORDED, not suppressed — and the difference is executable. `pnpm lint:migrations` PRINTS every
entry below as a NOTICE on each run, so an exempt finding is visible in the same output as a
failing one; it just does not fail the build. A NEW migration cannot join this list without an
owner editing this file, which is the point: the cost of an exception is a visible diff, not
silence. Tests keep it honest — every entry must name a real migration, rule and site with a
checkable reason, and none may be DEAD. ONE OF THE TWO ENTRIES IS A LIVE DEFECT on an
already-merged file: apps/api/prisma/** is read-only to this unit, so it is REPORTED, not
repaired, and needs its own unit.
A SECOND LIVE DEFECT — 20270920000000_decision_option_kinds:273 — has NO entry here and NO
backstop in this unit. It is detected only by MI-003, which is deferred at 08835700 on the
closed claude/migration-invariant-linter branch. An exemption for a rule that does not run
would suppress nothing and the no-dead-exemption test would refuse it. Deferring the rule did
not unfind the defect; it removed the alarm. See docs/MIGRATION_INVARIANTS.md.

20270225000000_phase4_t3_correction3.MI-001:167:5d27fbda47ce05f6: LIVE DEFECT — REPORTED, NOT FIXED. Line 167 verifies the prerequisite composite foreign keys by conname + conrelid + contype='f' + convalidated, and never reads pg_trigger.tgenabled on tgconstraint. This is exactly the a222e91 (PR #411) class: `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` leaves every column that guard reads unchanged while the keys stop enforcing, so a restored database with NO containment satisfies the prerequisite and is baselined as correct. apps/api/prisma/** is read-only to this unit, so this is recorded and reported rather than repaired here.

20270930000000_schedule_dependency_graph.MI-001:797:ca1c497dd20f3733: ACCEPTED — 1 site. Section 1e' (line 797) compares each foreign key's TARGET by confrelid OID and asks nothing about enforcement, which is what MI-001 reports. It is accepted because section 1e'' — the NEXT statement inside the SAME DO block, over the SAME five keys — asks the enforcement question per internal trigger and refuses tgenabled outside ('O','A'). THAT JUSTIFICATION IS ITSELF CROSS-SITE REASONING, which is exactly what MI-001 rejects, so it is sound here only for a reason that does not generalise: this migration is APPLIED and Prisma has recorded its checksum, so the file cannot change — the statement this acceptance leans on cannot be removed, reordered or weakened without a NEW migration, which MI-001 would judge on its own terms. On an unapplied file the same argument would be worthless: the neighbour could be deleted tomorrow and this site would still carry its exemption. The rule is not weakened to accommodate this; it does not read that neighbour on 1e''s behalf and must not, because that is precisely the coarser-than-the-site evidence PR #423 was closed for. The judgement is a human one, pinned to this exact query by its fingerprint, and written down here where a reviewer sees it.

__SCHEMA__: AN ENTRY EXEMPTS ONE SITE, where a site is ONE SQL QUERY as PostgreSQL's grammar sees it. The
key is "<RULE>:<line>:<fingerprint>" and ALL THREE parts must match the finding exactly.
This ledger was keyed by MIGRATION AND RULE alone until PR #430, which made it the THIRD
occurrence of one defect in this unit's lineage: PR #423 gathered a rule's evidence per FILE,
then per BLOCK, and was closed for it; the rule was then made per site and THE LEDGER THAT
OVERRIDES THE RULE was left coarser than the rule, so one accepted site silently discharged
every other MI-001 site in the same file — a genuinely defective one included. A ledger coarser
than the rule it overrides IS the rule at the coarser granularity.
THE CHOICE OF SITE IDENTIFIER, AND WHY IT IS BOTH:
line         WHERE. Migrations under apps/api/prisma/** are IMMUTABLE once applied — Prisma
records a checksum and refuses a changed file — so for a real entry the line does
not drift, and it is the half a reviewer can navigate to.
fingerprint  WHAT. sha-256 of the query's own text with whitespace runs collapsed, first 16
hex. The half with teeth: a CHANGED query must RE-EARN its exemption, because an
acceptance is written about one specific query, not about an address.
Neither alone was chosen, because neither alone is enough. Line alone lets an edited query inherit
an acceptance written for its predecessor — and immutability is a property of APPLIED migrations,
not of this file format, which is also used against directories the linter is pointed at.
Fingerprint alone exempts EVERY identical query in the file: the migration-global defect again,
wearing a hash. Requiring both means an entry stops applying the moment either half stops being
true, and `no exemption is dead` then fails it loudly. To read a site's key:
`node scripts/migration-lint.mjs` prints each finding.
THE AUDIT — the fix was not applied only where the finding pointed. Every place a verdict can be
suppressed or discharged, and its granularity:
the exemption lookup       PER SITE (this key). Was per migration+rule; corrected in PR #430.
`no exemption is dead`     PER SITE — it matches raised findings on this same key, so an entry
whose line OR fingerprint no longer binds is reported dead.
the rule's own evidence    PER SITE — MI-001 reads only its own query's parse tree.
run-time-built statements  PER SITE — pinned as an exact <migration>:<line> set, not a count,
so a new one names itself rather than moving a number.
the CLI's migration count  REPORT ONLY. It suppresses nothing; every finding prints its site.
